comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -38,13 +38,13 @@ paidInFull :: PaymentSignal -> Bool
 paidInFull = \case
   SigFunded _ f -> f == PaidInFull
   SigSettled {} -> True
-  SigClosed {} -> False
+  SigClosed _ f -> f == PaidInFull
comment.body: Same question for names, once they are sold through these invoices.

Support gets the order id from the buyer: the page shows it as "Reference" and asks them to quote it (`web/src/screens.ts:184`, `:775`), but they never see the code's hash. Could this label be the order id (`invId`, made just above), so support can search Stripe with what the buyer quotes and the code's hash stays in this service's database only? Showing the hash on the page instead would work too, but that's 72 characters to quote against a 22-character id. The order id is made once per request, so a retry inside the service would still send the same key.

@@ -235,27 +236,33 @@ instance J.FromJSON CreatedIntent where
 
 createInvoice :: StripeEnv -> ServicePaymentMethod -> OrderDraft -> IO (Either ProviderError ProviderInvoice)
 createInvoice _ (SPMCrypto _) _ = pure (Left (ProviderError "stripe offers no crypto payment method"))
-createInvoice env (SPMCard CPStripe) OrderDraft {odAmount = CurrencyAmount minor, odCurrency} = do
-  let form =
-        [ ("amount", B8.pack (show minor)),
-          ("currency", TE.encodeUtf8 (T.toLower odCurrency)),
+createInvoice env (SPMCard CPStripe) OrderDraft {odAmount = CurrencyAmount minor, odCurrency, odReference} = do
+  let amount = B8.pack (show minor)
+      currency = TE.encodeUtf8 (T.toLower odCurrency)
+      reference = TE.encodeUtf8 odReference
+      form =
+        [ ("amount", amount),
+          ("currency", currency),
           -- Only card is offered, because a redirect-based method would navigate the top window out of the embedded frame.
-          ("allowed_payment_method_types[]", "card")
+          ("allowed_payment_method_types[]", "card"),
+          ("metadata[order]", reference)
         ]
-  created <- stripeApi env what methodPost ["v1", "payment_intents"] [] (Just form)
+      -- Stripe answers a create sent again with the same key, for 24 hours, with the intent the first one made.
+      idempotencyKey = B8.intercalate ":" [reference, amount, currency]
comment.body:
This key only repeats when a create is sent again with the same code hash, and nothing sends one: the web page draws a new code for every attempt (`web/src/flow.ts:291`, `newCode()` inside the attempt loop), `stripeApi` sends each create once, and a code that already has rows is refused before Stripe is called (`codeHashExists`). So after a lost answer from Stripe the buyer's retry still creates a new intent. Nothing can be paid twice, since the first intent's client secret never reached the buyer.

Which retry is the key for? If it's a retry inside the service, could it come with this change? Note that Stripe stores the first answer for a key, an error included, and replays it for 24 hours.

issue.title: docs: parental controls design
issue.body:
Designs parental controls for the iPhone and Android apps: a parent PIN on a child's phone that keeps the child from connecting to new people, joining groups or searching the directory unless the parent allows it, and lets the parent switch off calls, files, voice and media.

Replaces #7019, which held the first draft of this design (May). This PR carries the same file, `plans/2026-05-27-parental-controls-design.md`, rewritten after a review against today's code on both platforms and against issue #4482 and its discussion, then adjusted to the decisions taken on it, with the app's screens drawn beside it. The two commits of #7019 are kept in the branch's history.

The design answers the second request of #4482: a parent PIN on the child's phone and approval before adding new contacts. It does not build the first request, forwarding the child's messages to a parent: nothing in it reads, keeps, shows or reports the child's chats.

What it proposes:
- A parent PIN of at least 6 digits, separate from the app lock, that guards seven switches: connecting to new people, groups and channels, and searching SimpleX Directory (#7881), off by default; calls, sending files, voice messages and receiving media, which the parent can switch off.
- "Allow once" with the PIN for connecting to someone new and for joining a group or channel; the parent sees the contact's or the group's name before approving.
- Contacts the parent marks as "Always allowed", such as the parents, keep calls, files, voice and media. The parent marks each one on that contact's page with the PIN, so the parent never sees the contact list.
- Each action the child starts checked in the app's function that sends it to the chat core, so every button that reaches it is covered, including future ones; buttons are hidden or disabled as well.
- A small in-memory parental mode in the core, set by the app at every start, for what the core does on its own: auto-accepting requests and invitations, ringing for incoming calls, receiving inline files. It reaches every profile, hidden ones included, and contacts connected incognito, without listing anything. One new local API command and one new error; no protocol, message or database format change.
- The PIN opens only the parental screen, "Allow once" and a contact's "Always allowed"; database export and migration, developer tools with the chat console, and "Use from desktop" are off while controls are on. The child's app lock, self-destruct and profiles stay the child's.
- "Parental controls on" in Settings; every refused action says "Turned off by parental controls"; nothing visible to contacts.
- Reinstalling the app removes the controls; on iPhone the setup explains how Screen Time stops app deletion. Phones only, not desktop.
- Screens for iOS, drawn from the views they extend, with the differences on Android: the privacy settings row, the parental screen before a PIN, during setup and on, the PIN pad, the alerts and approvals, the setup confirmation, Settings, a contact's page and a chat.

Two choices for the project owner are marked provisional in the document: connections started before the controls, and desktop. The PIN doesn't unlock the app: when the child has locked it, the parent asks the child to unlock it.

No code changes. The screens are drawn by hand from the iOS views they extend; none was built or run.
